reference_sql:
SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id, ecommerce.purchase_revenue AS purchase_revenue
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
  AND event_date = '20251202'
alternatives:
WITH day_purchases AS (
  -- one row per purchase event on the Dublin day 2 December 2025: its ID and its value parameter
  SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id, list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'value')[1].value AS v
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date = '20251202'
)
SELECT transaction_id, COALESCE(v.int_value, v.float_value, v.double_value) AS purchase_revenue
FROM day_purchases

SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id, ecommerce.purchase_revenue
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
  AND CAST(strptime(event_date, '%Y%m%d') AS DATE) = DATE '2025-12-02'

other_way.sql:
WITH day_purchases AS (
  -- one row per purchase event on the Dublin day 2 December 2025: its ID and its value parameter
  SELECT ecommerce.transaction_id AS transaction_id, list_filter(event_params, lambda p: p.key = 'value')[1].value AS v
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date = '20251202'
)
SELECT transaction_id, COALESCE(v.int_value, v.float_value, v.double_value) AS purchase_revenue
FROM day_purchases
other_way.tradeoff: The value parameter holds the same amount as purchase_revenue, but it must be read from whichever number slot holds it.
